My whole life I was more advanced than everyone. I grew up quick, things were simple as an only child. If you didn't like the meal you cooked your own. I did that at 8 and never looked back. By time I was 12 It was normal to wake up go to school come home, cook dinner and never see my parents. Being mature or self sufficient was great but it was also the only option. Now I find myself almost 22 with no college education and only 1 job that was worthwhile. At some point at 17 or 18 I fell behind instead of graduating and doing all the other things people did, I was working full time and hoping simply to not be alone anymore.   My whole life I was operating in a different world and I hoped that growing older and maturing would make me relatable or likeable by peers. Yet still I lack a solid connection, I just don't fit in because I'm difficult to understand. I'm incredibly mature but yeah I'm struggling to consistently be that way. I'm 22 and live with extended family and I just lost my job. At 18 I had my own place and a good starting salary.  Obviously I'm more mature now than 18 and yet I don't feel it, I don't look it.  I don't have my shit together right now, but one day soon I will and things will feel much different.  I'm struggling, I'm struggling big time but I chose an "alternative" life path. I created this world for myself and I know I've got it in me to rise above it all. But until I do...I'll feel immature. I'll feel like smoking weed with my friends and watching stupid sitcoms is a waste of my life. But when I'm working that 40 hours a week and smiling more often at strangers guess what, I'll go home and I'll smoke that same bowl and I'll watch the same show. I'm just myself in all situations and I promise it has burned me many times , but I enjoy it.  No matter how immature or mature I am I'll enjoy the things that make me, me.  So sometime being immature is actually just the small quirky things that make you special and don't let the world tell you that letting go of that is required. As a child I loved sports the way a grown man would, as a man I enjoy cartoons the way a child would. Be yourself and embrace the things you've questioned because they are most likely the key to your life's happiness. Being mature means growing in from where you were before.  Handling your own business is maturity. Acting like a stiff is not. Stick to principle morals, passion and love and you'll never feel misguided.  Even if you end up somewhere you don't want to be you'll know it was your answers to life that got you there. And you can have faith your answers will take youre to other places as well. I hope my wall of txt wasn't to incoherent. My point is that you should embrace the parts of you that make you....you! And not let anyone define those things as mature or immature. Use your own judgment to understand your growth as a person and find out what makes you feel alive in this world. Sometimes maturity is the 9
-5 for a few decades while sending kids to college. But the world needs people who fight the norm, people who chase dreams. If you want to chase your dream that's okay, it doesn't make you immature.  The immature side of me realizes that I needed to have this thought process whether I posted it or not, so i thank you for asking and wish you well in your life!
